content:
maya.ng: quick sync before we enable `kai-7b-v3` in catalog. change window tonight 22:00-02:00 UTC. primary concerns: fallback ordering, pin/unpin, and memory churn from quant variants.

jordan: +1. propose fallback order: `kai-7b-v3-quant` -> `kai-7b-v2` -> `tiny-250m`. quant first reduces cost but we need TTL to avoid cache thrash.

ops_oncall: what's a safe TTL? if too short we'll see cold-starts; too long we waste memory. suggest 12h default, override per-region.

maya.ng: thinking 6h for eu regions, 12h for us. we'll make it runtime-configurable. also plan pin duration 90m during canary.

nora: rollback triggers: p95 latency > 300ms for 10m, request error rate > 6% sustained 5m, or quality regression on canary eval set > 2.5%. Owner: model-rt lead + ops.

samuel.l: deploybot, schedule canary. region eu-west1 @ 22:15 UTC 4% traffic, then ap-south1 @ 22:40 UTC 4%, ramp plan to 25% over 75m if green.

deploybot: @samuel.l scheduled: `catalog.enable(kai-7b-v3)` canaries: eu-west1 1766993695 (4%), ap-south1 1766995200 (4%). ramp checkpoints: 30m/60m/75m. Logs -> #eng-releases. :mechanical_arm:

jordan: ops note 1: pin autoscaler to reserved pool for the canary; drain before final switch. add drain_before_unpin = true.

maya.ng: code snippet for ops:
```json
{"pin": ["kai-7b-v3", "kai-7b-v3-quant"], "pin_duration":"90m", "drain_before_unpin": true, "fallback_ttl": {"eu-west1":"6h","ap-south1":"12h","us-central1":"12h"}}
```

nora: make sure monitoring will surface token-cost delta and prefix-cache hit rate. also add a synthetic load test at minute 20.

samuel.l: adding synthetic: 200 reqs/min across sampled routes, compare top-k tokens distribution to baseline. fail fast if deviation > 4%.

ops_oncall: oncall schedule: i'm primary until 23:30, @jordan takes over afterwards. will join rollback call if alerts fire.

maya.ng: decision ladder: pass minute-30 checkpoint -> continue; fail -> immediate rollback to `kai-7b-v2` and clear pins. manual confirm required for >25% ramp.

jordan: small tweak: if quant variant TTL eviction causes cold-start latency > 1.5x baseline, reduce TTL to 1h and pin only the non-quant model. ops, be ready to execute.

deploybot: preflight checks done: artifact checksums match, model signature validated, quant benchmark within perf window.

nora: adding the release note to internal changelog: includes new safety config, fallback ordering, default TTL per region, pin/unpin behaviour, and rollback criteria.

maya.ng: I'll be watching the canary at 22:15. ping here if anything anomalous. :eyes:

samuel.l: starting the canary now. job id 908172. stream: https://deploy.redwood/908172

jordan: seeing a tiny spike at t+3m (p95 +8%) but it normalizes. tagging for context.

ops_oncall: memory stable, quant cache hit 68%. synthetic load at minute 20 shows <2% deviation. continuing to 25%.

nora: regen eval batch 1 passed quality checks. no user-visible regressions so far.

maya.ng: if 75m checkpoint passes, schedule unpin 30m before full ramp. don't forget to set drain window to 10m.

samuel.l: copy that. unpin scheduled at 23:40 UTC, drain starts 23:50 UTC.

deploybot: canary progressed to 25% across regions. no critical alerts. job id 908172 still active.

jordan: final note: ensure the fallback chain TTL is returned in the catalog API so clients can reason about eviction. small enhancement but useful.

maya.ng: agreed. logging this as follow-up. thanks all, standing down unless pager lights up.
